tasks.title: Make build_type dir-driven (loosen the schema enum)
tasks.description: Change build_type in contracts/schemas/v1/requirements.schema.json from the closed enum [game,cli,app,library,other] to a format-validated slug string (pattern ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$, optional). The templates/ directory plus scaffold's existing 'no template for build_type' error remain the real gate. Verify the custom validator enforces the pattern (and drop any enum special-casing in cli/lib/validate.js if present). Test-first.
acceptance_criteria: build_type is declared as an optional slug-pattern string; the closed enum is gone.
plan compile accepts a valid slug build_type (e.g. cli, library) and a requirements.json with no build_type, and rejects a malformed value (e.g. "Not A Slug").
Existing cli and scaffold-phase requirements still validate; a test covers valid/omitted/invalid cases; full suite passes.

tasks.title: Author the library build-type template
tasks.description: Create templates/library/template.json (valid against template.schema.json, required_files listed) and templates/library/files/: package.json (name {{slug}}, main src/index.js, no bin, test script), README.md, .gitignore, src/index.js exporting a sample function, test/index.test.js exercising it. Only {{slug}}/{{summary}} placeholders; only node: built-ins. A test renders the template into a temp project and asserts required_files are produced and the report validates.
acceptance_criteria: templates/library/template.json validates against template.schema.json and lists its required_files.
Scaffolding build_type=library renders the files/ tree with {{slug}}/{{summary}} substituted and writes a valid scaffold-report.json.
The rendered test/index.test.js passes under node --test; a framework test covers the render; full suite passes.

tasks.title: Author the app build-type template
tasks.description: Create templates/app/template.json and templates/app/files/: package.json (name {{slug}}, start script 'node src/server.js', test script), README.md, .gitignore, src/server.js exporting a request handler and a start(port) helper using node:http, test/server.test.js that binds an ephemeral port (listen(0)), makes one request and asserts the response. acceptance_criteria: templates/app/template.json validates against template.schema.json and lists its required_files.

The rendered server test binds an ephemeral port and passes under node --test with zero dependencies; full suite passes.

tasks.title: Add the `appbuilder templates` discovery command
tasks.description: Add cli/lib/templates.js exporting listTemplates(cwd) that scans templates/*/template.json, and dispatch `appbuilder templates [--json]` from the router. Default output is a human-readable list of id / name / description; --json emits the structured list (matching the status command pattern). Skips non-template entries (e.g. .gitkeep) gracefully. Test-first.
acceptance_criteria: appbuilder templates lists every templates/<id>/ with a valid manifest (cli, library, app, game) showing id, name, description.
appbuilder templates --json emits a valid structured list; both modes ignore .gitkeep and malformed entries without crashing.
A test asserts the command lists the known templates in both modes; full suite passes and doctor is green.

tasks.title: Document templates and the dir-driven build_type
tasks.description: Add an 'authoring a template' recipe (folder layout, template.json contract, the {{slug}}/{{summary}} variables, required_files, 'a folder is all it takes'). Update HOWTO.md and README.md scaffold sections to mention `appbuilder templates` and the open build_type, and update .agent/plan-interview.md to point at the live `appbuilder templates` list instead of a hardcoded enum. Docs only.
acceptance_criteria: A template-authoring recipe documents the folder layout, manifest contract, substitution variables, and required_files.
HOWTO.md/README.md mention `appbuilder templates` and the dir-driven build_type; .agent/plan-interview.md points at the live list rather than a fixed enum.
No stale 'no template for X yet' or closed-enum language remains where it is now wrong; full suite passes (docs-only change).
